title: Talking About the Past: Regular Verbs
summary: Learn how to talk about things that happened yesterday or last year. You will use easy spelling rules for regular verbs.

sections.p: We use the past simple to talk about finished actions in the past. For regular verbs, we make the past form very easily. We just add '-ed' to the end of the action word. It is the same for 'I', 'you', 'he', 'she', 'we', and 'they'.

ex.en: I walked to the store yesterday.
ex.mean: I went to the store on foot in the past.
They played a game of football in the past.

sections.p: Some action words already end with the letter 'e'. For these verbs, you do not need to add '-ed'. You only need to add a letter 'd' to the end. This makes writing and spelling much faster and easier for you.

ex.mean: She enjoyed the movie in the past.
Our home was in London during the year 2020.

sections.h: Spelling Rules: Verbs Ending in Consonant + 'Y'
sections.p: When a verb ends with a consonant letter and the letter 'y', we change the 'y' to 'i'. Then, we add '-ed'. For example, 'study' becomes 'studied'. But if there is a vowel before the 'y', like in 'play', just add '-ed'.

ex.en: She cried when she was sad.
ex.mean: Tears came from her eyes in the past.

tip: Look for words like 'yesterday' or 'last week'. When you see them, remember to change your verb to the past simple form!
